title: Priority denylist and soft-eviction profiles for noisy tenants
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Design and implement a priority-driven denylist plus configurable soft-eviction profiles to reduce noisy-tenant blast radius during regional congestion or degraded capacity. Goal is to provide fast, operator-safe controls that (1) block or deprioritize pathological traffic patterns, (2) apply tenant-specific graceful degradation templates (response trimming, model slimming, reduced beam/length caps), and (3) surface signals to automated admission controllers and the Console.

Motivation: During the last multi-region incident we saw a small set of tenants that generated high-cost long-stream requests causing headroom exhaustion in critical shards. Existing token-bucket and lane policies did not reduce tail load quickly enough and manual evictions were error-prone. A denylist-like quick-path plus per-tenant soft-eviction profile will reduce mean time to protect core customers and allow safe rollback.

Scope:
- Admission-level denylist with short TTLs for rapid protection (API-layer, region-local).
- Soft-eviction profiles stored in tenant metadata: ordered list of degradation actions (trim, quantize, model-variant fallback, no-streaming) with per-action parameters.
- Operator API in Console to apply a denylist entry or a profile to tenant(s) with canary and rollout percentages.
- Metrics and alerting hooks (SLO impact, eviction count, rejected requests, recovery time).
- Integration with existing predictive-shedder to automatically suggest profiles when anomalies are detected (future work).

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Denylist vs full blackhole: denylist entries are short-lived and include a reason and escalation path; prefer soft-degrades where possible to preserve degraded but functional behavior. Trade-off: short-term customer friction vs preventing total outage for others.
- Placement: denylist admission check should be as early as possible (API ingress) to avoid wasting downstream GPU cycles. Soft-eviction profiles are applied during routing/admission and may require model-variant mapping.
- Granularity: per-tenant, per-route and per-region keys supported. We will start with per-tenant-region scope.
- Observability: attach eviction_tag to traces and add a per-tenant eviction timeline in Console.

Implementation plan (high-level):
1) Data model and storage: add denylist and profiles to tenant metadata in ConfigDB (schema v3).
2) Admission integration: extend admission controller with denylist fast-path; apply profile hints to runtime router.
3) Runtime adapters: implement profile action handlers (trim, apply-quantized-variant, reduce-beams, disable-streaming).
4) Console: quick-action UI to apply denylist/profile with canary % and reason.
5) Telemetry: Grafana panels, SLO dashboards, and a PagerDuty runbook entry.

Rollout plan:
- Dev: unit + integration tests, local e2e harness with a synthetic noisy-tenant generator (2 weeks).
- Staged deploy: canary on non-production region (10% traffic) for 48h, monitor 95/99 P99 latency, error rate, and SLO burn.
- Production: roll to control plane, enable denylist only for selected operators for 1 week, then open to SRE.

Success metrics:
- 80% reduction in headroom exhaustion incidents caused by top-5 noisy tenants in test runs.
- <5% collateral SLO regressions for protected tenants during canary.
- Operator time-to-protect (apply denylist) < 3 minutes from detection.

Runbook and docs:
- Confluence design spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/priority-denylist-and-soft-evict-profiles (draft)
- Runbook stub: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/eviction-runbook
- Grafana dashboard (evictions and SLOs): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/evictions/tenant-evictions

Security/Compliance: Profiles may include model variant selection; ensure model choices are only to variants that satisfy tenant data controls. No changes to KMS.

Open questions:
- Should denylist entries be auto-generated by anomaly-detector or manual-first? (Prefer manual-first for Q1 rollout).
- Exact TTL defaults and escalation policy.
- How to represent compound actions in profile (e.g., trim + quantize + fallback)?

Next steps:
- RFC review with SRE and Console (scheduled 2024-11-18).
- Implementation spike: small PoC for denylist fast-path (owner: Marcus Li) due 2024-11-30.
